items.title: GHARP: Real-Time Gaussian Head Animation from Large-Scale Reconstruction Prior
items.abstract: We present GHARP (Real-time Gaussian Head Animation from Large-scale Reconstruction Prior), a method that animates 3D human heads in real time from a few input images of a subject and a driving expression signal. We decouple the problem into an identity stage that builds a representation of the subject’s geometry and appearance offline, and an animation stage that predicts expression-dependent residuals on top of it at runtime. This separation offers a favorable trade-off with respect to fidelity, quality and runtime: the identity stage can be expensive while the animation stage runs a…
items.title_ko: Apple, GHARP 공개 — 소수 이미지로 실시간 3D 얼굴 애니메이션, 신원·표정 단계 분리
items.summary: GHARP는 피사체의 입력 이미지 몇 장과 구동 표정 신호로부터 3D 사람 머리를 실시간으로 애니메이션하는 방법이다. 문제를 두 단계로 분리하는데, 오프라인에서 피사체의 기하와 외형 표현을 구축하는 신원 단계와, 런타임에 그 위에 표정 의존적 잔차를 예측하는 애니메이션 단계로 나눈다. 이 분리 구조는 **신원 단계는 비용이 들더라도 애니메이션 단계는 가볍게** 실행할 수 있어 품질, 충실도, 실행 속도 사이의 균형을 유리하게 가져간다.
items.why_it_matters: 실시간 3D 아바타 생성은 화상회의, 게임, AR/VR 등에 직접 적용 가능한 핵심 기술로, 가벼운 런타임 연산이 실용성을 좌우한다.
items.whats_different: 신원 정보를 오프라인에서 미리 구축하고 런타임에는 표정 잔차만 예측하는 **단계 분리 구조**를 통해 실시간성과 품질을 동시에 확보한다는 점이 특징이다.

items.title: Making Failure Diagnosis Reliable with Pensive AI
items.abstract: By Praneeth Yenugutala , Victor Dusa , Anastasia Samoilova , Megan Ren , Justin Wei , Marcelo Mayworm At Netflix, data and machine learning practitioners run millions of workloads each day across orchestration systems and compute engines such as Titus, Spark, Trino, and Druid. On peak days, roughly 100,000 workloads fail. When workloads fail, the failure itself is only the beginning. Someone still needs to find the useful signal in several logs, decide whether the cause sits in their code or the platform, and determine whether to retry, reconfigure, or escalate. Even a small share of difficult failures can consume engineering time, waste compute, and interrupt critical data pipelines. Our first answer to that problem was Pensive , an auto-diagnosis and remediation system in Netflix’s data platform. Pensive collected logs from failed workloads, used regular expressions and hand-authored Java rules to extract and classify errors, then passed retry or remediation guidance to products such as Maestro . It made ~ 50% of failures self-service and, in some cases, automatic. Rules work well for known patterns, but their coverage grows only when someone recognizes a new failure mode, understands the logs, writes a rule, and keeps it current as engines and log formats change. Over one three-month period, Pensive processed roughly seven million job-failure classifications, yet about half fell into the unknown bucket. We needed a way to expand coverage without giving up the deterministic parts of Pensive that already worked. To solve this ambiguous and complex problem at Netflix scale, we invested in Pensive AI to add AI-assisted error extractions and focused diagnosis and remediation guidance to our data and ML practitioners. The goal was not simply to place a model in front of a large collection of logs. We needed bounded extraction, predictable evaluation inputs, responsive product behavior, and quality checks that could follow the system from local development through production. Those requirements shaped every layer of the design, which we will discuss in this blog. Pensive AI wraps AI around deterministic processes, which gives broader coverage, low latency, controlled AI costs, and easier maintenance across the software development lifecycle. Building on this foundation, we plan to explore more agentic debugging experiences, as Part 6 describes. Early results are encouraging. AI error extraction now covers 100% of failures, including the failures that legacy Pensive classified as unknown. Failed step attempts where no one used Pensive AI averaged 321% more manual debug-log exploration actions than attempts where someone did (an observational comparison, not a causal claim). Figure 1. Pensive AI architecture. Always-on error extraction and on-demand debugging complement each other and share log sources, the LLM gateway, tracing, and the cache. Archived logs feed offline evals and release gates. The two paths complement each other. Error extraction improves an existing capability and is always on. It lets the user of a failed Maestro workload quickly check the parts of the logs that may point to an immediate root cause. It has low latency and low cost, and it can help in a large share of cases. On-demand debugging enables a new capability. It looks at symptoms across the logs and adds the LLM’s own knowledge and reasoning for a deeper analysis, at slightly higher latency and cost. Extraction gives a fast first look at every failure, and on-demand debugging triggered by the user goes deeper when that first look is not enough. Part 1: Finding the useful errors Legacy Pensive rules are precise, but each one captures a particular log shape. A simplified rule looks like this: - name: SparkContainerOOM logSource: GENIE_STDERR restartable: false regex: "Container.*is running beyond physical memory limits.*Killing container" summary: Spark AM container runs out of memory With Pensive AI, we wanted to find useful errors that had no correspond
items.title_ko: Netflix, 'Pensive AI'로 실패 진단 커버리지 확대 — 미분류 장애 0%, 수동 로그 탐색 321% 감소
items.summary: Netflix는 하루 약 10만 건의 워크로드 실패를 처리하기 위해 정규식과 Java 규칙 기반의 자동 진단 시스템 Pensive를 운영해왔으며, 이는 실패의 **약 50%**를 셀프서비스화했다. 그러나 3개월간 약 700만 건의 분류 중 절반가량이 '미분류'로 남는 한계가 있었다. 이를 해결하기 위해 AI 기반 오류 추출과 진단 가이드를 결합한 Pensive AI를 도입했고, 기존 규칙 기반 시스템의 결정론적 장점은 유지하면서 범위를 확장했다. 그 결과 AI 오류 추출이 **실패의 100%**를 커버하게 되었고, 온디맨드 디버깅 기능도 함께 제공한다.
items.why_it_matters: 대규모 플랫폼에서 규칙 기반 자동화의 한계(새로운 실패 패턴에 대한 커버리지 확장의 어려움)를 LLM으로 보완하면서도 비용과 지연시간을 통제한 실제 운영 사례라는 점에서 MLOps 실무자에게 참고할 가치가 있다.
items.whats_different: 기존 Pensive의 정규식·수동 작성 Java 규칙 기반 분류 대비, Pensive AI는 결정론적 추출 구조는 유지한 채 AI를 그 위에 결합하여 미분류 실패까지 커버하는 점이 다르다.

items.title: Fleet-wide computer vision lifecycle at the edge with SageMaker SDK v3
items.abstract: Fleet-wide computer vision model lifecycle management is a problem that shows up the moment a quality inspection proof of concept succeeds. One camera and one model work fine. Then the plant asks for the same result on 40 lines, each with several cameras, and every camera sees the world differently. Each has a different angle, different glare off the same stainless surface, and different ambient light depending on which bay door is open. In production deployments we have worked on, a single model trained on pooled footage underperforms enough individual cameras that each camera ends up with its own fine-tuned model. Now the real problem is no longer training one model well. It’s training, evaluating, versioning, and shipping thousands of them without a human in the loop for each one. This post updates the pattern introduced in the 2023 series Build an end-to-end MLOps pipeline for visual quality inspection at the edge for the current Amazon SageMaker Python SDK v3. It replaces the since-deprecated Amazon SageMaker Edge Manager with Amazon SageMaker Neo for edge optimization. I walk through a dual-branch Amazon SageMaker Pipeline that trains an anomaly detector and a defect classifier per camera, with quality gates that block underperforming models. An in-pipeline SageMaker Neo compilation step ensures every registered model ships with a device-optimized artifact, and an AWS Step Functions orchestration layer paces fleet training. You deploy everything with the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK), and a full pipeline run on synthetic data costs about $0.07 in compute. The complete sample is available in the aws-samples GitHub repository . Solution overview The following diagram shows the sample’s fleet-wide model lifecycle. An orchestration layer queues re-training requests and limits concurrent work. A per-camera training pipeline prepares data, trains and evaluates an anomaly detector and a classifier, and produces versioned model artifacts for edge devices. Figure 1: Solution architecture The training half is a single SageMaker Pipeline, parameterized by camera, that runs 13 steps per execution. Three entry steps run in parallel: Preprocess, Fetch Latest Anomaly, and Fetch Latest Classifier. The pipeline preprocesses that camera’s images and fetches the camera’s most recent approved model for each branch, then trains two models. The first is a small convolutional autoencoder that learns what normal product looks like and flags anomalies by reconstruction error. The second is a ResNet18 classifier fine-tuned to confirm the defect. Each branch exports its model to ONNX, evaluates the exported artifact against held-out data, and passes through a quality gate. Past the gate, the model is compiled with SageMaker Neo for the configured edge target, and only then registered in the SageMaker Model Registry. As a result, every approved package has a device-ready compiled artifact. Packages carry the camera ID as metadata, and each branch’s warm-start fetch filters on it, so re-training always resumes from that camera’s own history. The orchestration half paces the fleet. Re-training requests land on an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue, and an AWS Lambda function starts a Step Functions execution per request. Each execution acquires a slot through a DynamoDB semaphore before starting its pipeline, so a burst of requests drains at a steady rate instead of all launching at once. Completions publish to Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS), and operational failures reach the same topic through an Amazon EventBridge rule with the original error preserved. The output of the system is versioned, quality-gated, per-camera model artifacts. The Model Registry holds the portable ONNX, and S3 holds the Neo-compiled build of that model, which is a device-optimized shared library loaded by the DLR runtime rather than ONNX. Both are ready for whatever delivery mechanism your plant uses. Prerequisites To deploy the sampl

items.summary: 공장 내 수십 개 라인, 각각 여러 대의 카메라에서 품질 검사를 할 때 단일 모델은 성능이 부족해 카메라마다 별도로 파인튜닝된 모델이 필요해진다는 문제에서 출발한다. 이 글은 카메라별로 오토인코더 기반 이상탐지기와 ResNet18 결함 분류기를 학습·평가·버전관리·배포하는 13단계 **SageMaker Pipeline**을 제시하며, 품질 게이트를 통과한 모델만 ONNX로 내보내 SageMaker Neo로 엣지용 컴파일 후 Model Registry에 등록한다. AWS Step Functions와 SQS, DynamoDB 세마포어로 구성된 오케스트레이션 레이어가 재학습 요청을 큐잉하고 동시 실행 수를 제한해 전체 카메라 군의 학습 속도를 조절한다. 합성 데이터 기준 전체 파이프라인 1회 실행 비용은 **약 0.07달러**이며, AWS CDK로 전체 인프라를 배포한다.
items.why_it_matters: PoC 단계에서 통하던 단일 모델이 현장 배치에서는 카메라별 각도·조명 차이로 성능이 떨어지는 현상은 컴퓨터 비전 엣지 배포에서 흔히 겪는 실전 문제이며, 사람 개입 없이 수천 개 모델을 관리하는 패턴은 제조업 MLOps에 바로 적용 가능하다.
items.whats_different: 2023년 공개된 기존 패턴에서 더 이상 지원되지 않는 **Amazon SageMaker Edge Manager**를 SageMaker Neo로 교체하고 SDK v3에 맞게 업데이트한 버전이다.

items.title: DISC: Domain-Integrated Similarity Cost for Time-Series Dataset
items.abstract: The growth of time-series datasets and foundation models has made dataset comparison a central part of time-series workflows. Assessing source-target transfer before model adaptation requires similarity estimates that can summarize transfer-related dataset relationships without exhaustive source-target evaluation over every candidate pair. Many metrics have been proposed for measuring similarity between time-series datasets, but they capture different dataset relationships and vary in how well they align with downstream utility across tasks. We evaluate this gap by measuring the correlation between source-target similarity scores and downstream forecasting errors in out-of-distribution and transfer-learning settings. We propose Domain-Integrated Similarity Cost (DISC), a learnable aggregation framework that uses calibration transfer observations to select, weight, and combine similarity metrics for different downstream tasks. By integrating complementary metric values, DISC better distinguishes source-target dataset differences that matter for downstream behavior. After calibration, DISC scores source-target pairs using only their similarity-metric values and yields higher alignment than single-metric references on the reported split. These results show that time-series dataset similarity is task-dependent, and that learned metric integration provides a stronger proxy for downstream transfer behavior than manually selecting one similarity metric.
items.title_ko: DISC: 여러 유사도 지표를 학습 결합해 시계열 데이터셋 전이 적합성 예측 정확도 향상
items.summary: 시계열 기초모델 확산으로 소스-타겟 데이터셋 간 전이 적합성을 사전 평가할 필요가 커졌지만, 기존 단일 유사도 지표들은 과업마다 다운스트림 성능과의 상관관계가 제각각이다. 저자들은 소스-타겟 유사도 점수와 분포 외·전이학습 환경에서의 예측 오차 간 상관관계를 측정해 이 문제를 분석했다. 이를 바탕으로 여러 유사도 지표를 보정용 전이 관측치로 학습해 선택·가중·결합하는 프레임워크인 **DISC**를 제안한다. 보정 후에는 유사도 지표 값만으로 소스-타겟 쌍을 평가하며, 보고된 분할에서 단일 지표 기준보다 더 높은 정렬도를 보였다.
items.why_it_matters: 시계열 기초모델을 특정 도메인에 적용하기 전, 전수 평가 없이도 어떤 소스 데이터가 타겟 전이에 유리한지 미리 판단할 수 있는 실용적 방법이 필요한 시점에서 의미가 크다.
items.whats_different: **단일 유사도 지표를 수작업으로 선택**하던 기존 방식과 달리, DISC는 여러 지표를 과업별로 학습 결합해 다운스트림 전이 성능과의 정렬도를 높인다.

items.title: Co-adaptive Rule Routing and Constraining for Structured Knowledge Retrieval
items.abstract: Structured knowledge retrieval acquires task-relevant evidence from structured knowledge sources for downstream tasks. Existing methods rely on unconstrained retrieval or predefined query-rule supervision, such as author-paper rules for scientific discovery and anatomy-drug rules for precision medicine. Such supervision is rarely available in practice. We propose Co-Adaptive Rule Routing and Constraining Retrieval (CoRE), which jointly learns which reasoning rule to assign to each query and how to retrieve evidence under that rule, without predefined query-rule pairs. A routing agent selects a rule, and its corresponding retriever traverses the knowledge base and ranks evidence that satisfies the rule's constraints. Because routing and retrieval are interdependent, CoRE alternates between reinforcement learning for the routing policy and contrastive learning for the rule-constrained retriever. The selected rules provide supervision for retriever training, while retrieval performance rewards the routing policy. This closed-loop process enables both components to co-adapt without explicit query-rule supervision. Experiments on STaRK-QA datasets across scientific discovery, biomedical reasoning, and e-commerce knowledge management demonstrate CoRE's effectiveness. Ablations show the benefit of co-adapting the router and retriever. Generation-based routing transfers across datasets and benefits from multi-domain pretraining followed by target-specific fine-tuning. Analysis of rule usage across queries also informs automatic rule refinement and discovery.
items.title_ko: CoRE 제안 — 쿼리-규칙 쌍 없이 라우팅·검색 공동학습, STaRK-QA 전 도메인서 구조적 지식 검색 개선
items.summary: 이 논문은 구조화된 지식 검색을 위해 CoRE(Co-Adaptive Rule Routing and Constraining Retrieval)라는 방법을 제안한다. 기존 방식은 비제약 검색이나 저자-논문, 해부학-약물 같은 사전 정의된 쿼리-규칙 지도 데이터가 필요했지만, CoRE는 이런 사전 쌍 없이 각 쿼리에 어떤 추론 규칙을 할당할지와 해당 규칙 하에서 증거를 어떻게 검색할지를 함께 학습한다. 라우팅 에이전트가 규칙을 선택하면, 해당 검색기가 지식베이스를 탐색해 규칙 제약을 만족하는 증거를 순위화하며, **강화학습 기반 라우팅 정책**과 대조학습 기반 검색기 학습을 번갈아 수행하는 폐루프 구조로 두 요소가 공동 적응한다. 과학적 발견, 생의학 추론, 전자상거래 지식관리 등 STaRK-QA 데이터셋 실험에서 효과를 입증했으며, 라우터와 검색기의 공동 적응이 성능에 기여함을 어블레이션으로 확인했다. 생성 기반 라우팅은 데이터셋 간 전이가 가능하고 다중 도메인 사전학습 후 타겟 특화 미세조정에서 이점을 보였다.
items.why_it_matters: 쿼리-규칙 지도 데이터가 실제로는 거의 구비되지 않는다는 현실적 제약을 해소함으로써, 과학적 발견이나 정밀의료처럼 구조화된 지식베이스를 다루는 다양한 응용 분야에 적용 가능성을 넓힌다.
items.whats_different: 기존의 비제약 검색이나 저자-논문, 해부학-약물 같은 **사전 정의된 쿼리-규칙 지도** 방식과 달리, CoRE는 라우팅 정책과 규칙 제약 검색기를 사전 쌍 없이 강화학습-대조학습 교대 방식으로 동시에 학습한다.

items.title: Soloists, Copy-Pasters, and Tourists
items.abstract: Spend a week with almost any infrastructure team in 2026 and you’ll see one AI subscription producing five very different results. One engineer opens 40 pull requests before lunch across repositories they haven’t touched in a year. Another ships a Terraform change they couldn’t explain in a code review. A third hasn’t opened the tool since the pilot and says they’ll come back “when it’s ready.” A fourth uses it for two narrow jobs, decoding a SAML trace and writing a regex they never want to write by hand again, and may be the most productive person on the team. The fifth tried it in March and again in June, and will try it again after the next keynote. The usual way to describe this is Everett Rogers’s diffusion curve : innovators, early adopters, early majority, late majority, laggards. Rogers’s framework measures when people adopt. It says nothing about how they use a tool once they have it, and with AI that’s where the outcomes split. The engineer with 40 PRs and the one with two use cases are both early adopters, but they achieve different results and create different types of risk for the team. None of the five types Rogers described is new. Previous technology shifts, from the PC and the web to Stack Overflow and the cloud, produced similar behavior. AI just changes where the bottleneck sits. The bottleneck moved For most of software’s history, writing code was slow, so development methods focused on managing that work. Waterfall put the planning up front because changing course late was expensive. However, even in the 1970 paper that’s usually cited as the origin of waterfall, Winston Royce warned that the strictly sequential version was “risky and invites failure.” The industry skipped the warning and adopted the diagram. Agile was the correction. The 2001 Agile Manifesto prioritized “responding to change over following a plan,” and short iterations replaced yearlong specifications. The manifesto still valued the plan, but that part got skipped too. Facebook took the idea to its limit with “move fast and break things.” At its F8 conference in 2014, it retired the slogan in favor of “move fast with stable infra,” because fixing what broke had started to cost more time than the speed saved. AI has now sped up what was left. Models draft the code, and since GitHub made Copilot code review generally available in April 2025, a model often reviews it too. The tempting response is to push Agile further, with shorter loops, more agents, and less ceremony. In other words, break things faster. But when one engineer can open 40 PRs a day, the cumulative changes can leave the team with a system nobody can reason about. The better position is somewhere between the two. It isn’t waterfall’s fixed specification, but it isn’t the absence of one either. It means a roadmap that says where the team is going and why, issues that state the problem before anyone generates a solution, and design reviews where people argue about trade-offs. That structure looks like it would slow things down, but it’s what makes speed safe. Jazz musicians can improvise freely because everyone on the bandstand knows the chord changes and the form of the tune. Without that framing, they’d just be making noise. A roadmap does the same job for a team of people and their agents. It sets the boundaries, and inside them everyone can move as fast as the tools allow. With AI accelerating implementation, planning is now the only part that decides whether the fast parts are worth doing. On my blog Synthetic Auth , I’ve called this the difference between conducting and auditing . A Conductor holds the “why” (the requirements, the history, the users) and directs agents toward a “how” that fits it. An Auditor hands over a ticket, checks that the code runs and the tests pass, and ships it. Both can end up with the same diff, but only the Conductor knows whether it solves the actual problem. An AI reviewer can’t tell the two apart because it only sees the diff, not the inte
items.title_ko: O'Reilly 칼럼 — AI 시대 개발자 5유형 분석, 병목은 코딩에서 '기획'으로 이동
items.summary: 같은 AI 구독 도구를 쓰고도 팀 내 엔지니어들은 하루 40개 PR을 올리는 사람부터 도구를 거의 쓰지 않는 사람까지 전혀 다른 결과를 낸다. 저자는 Rogers의 기술 수용 주기(혁신가·초기 수용자 등)가 '언제 쓰는가'만 설명할 뿐 '어떻게 쓰는가'는 설명하지 못한다고 지적한다. Waterfall에서 Agile, Facebook의 'move fast and break things'까지 소프트웨어 개발 방법론은 항상 코딩 속도라는 병목을 관리해왔지만, **AI가 구현 속도를 극도로 높이면서 이제 병목은 기획과 로드맵으로 옮겨갔다**. 저자는 요구사항과 맥락을 쥐고 에이전트를 지휘하는 'Conductor'와 단순히 티켓을 넘기고 결과물만 확인하는 'Auditor'를 구분하며, AI 리뷰어는 diff만 볼 뿐 그 둘을 구별하지 못한다고 설명한다.
items.why_it_matters: AI 도입이 빨라질수록 코드 생산 속도보다 '무엇을, 왜 만드는가'를 정하는 기획·로드맵 역량이 팀 성과를 가르는 핵심 변수가 된다는 점에서, 단순 도구 보급률이 아니라 활용 방식에 주목해야 함을 시사한다.
items.whats_different: 기존 Rogers의 기술 수용 주기 모델 대비, 이 글은 '언제 도입했는가'가 아니라 '도입 후 어떻게 사용하는가'에 따라 동일한 초기 수용자 집단 안에서도 성과와 위험이 크게 갈린다는 점을 강조한다.

items.title: FLORA: An Open Model Suite for Scaling Robotics Data Engines
items.abstract: The life-cycle of robotics foundation models crucially depends on data labels. Outcome reward labels are needed for monitoring real-world deployments. Process reward labels are needed during RL post-training. Timestamped captions are needed for filtering and balancing pretraining data. We present Flora, an industrial-quality data engine used for training GR00T models, that simultaneously covers these capabilities. Flora achieves SOTA scores on the captioning benchmark WGO-Bench and reward benchmarks RoboReward and Robometer. On internal benchmarks it is competitive with GPT-6 Astra while beating other frontier models. The model is substantially cheaper than API-based alternatives, roughly 125 times cheaper than GPT-6 Astra. Florais battle tested at scale, labeling 200,000 hours of data per day across 512 GB300s. By open-sourcing our data engine, we enable researchers to scale custom robotics datasets and explore emerging applications such as physical auto-research and human-to-robot transfer.
items.title_ko: Flora 공개 — GR00T 학습용 로보틱스 데이터 엔진, WGO-Bench 등 SOTA에 GPT-6 Astra 대비 125배 저렴
items.summary: Flora는 로보틱스 파운데이션 모델 학습에 필요한 결과 보상, 과정 보상, 타임스탬프 캡션 레이블을 동시에 생성하는 산업용 데이터 엔진으로, GR00T 모델 학습에 사용됐다. 캡션 벤치마크 WGO-Bench와 보상 벤치마크 RoboReward, Robometer에서 **SOTA 성능**을 달성했다. 내부 벤치마크에서는 GPT-6 Astra와 대등하거나 다른 프런티어 모델들을 능가하며, API 기반 대안보다 **약 125배 저렴**하다. 512개의 GB300 장비로 하루 20만 시간 분량의 데이터를 레이블링하는 규모로 실전 검증됐다.
items.why_it_matters: 로보틱스 모델 학습은 레이블링 비용과 품질에 크게 좌우되는데, 이를 오픈소스로 공개하면 연구자들이 커스텀 로보틱스 데이터셋을 저비용으로 확장하고 물리적 자동 연구, 인간-로봇 전이 같은 새로운 응용을 탐색할 수 있게 된다.
items.whats_different: **GPT-6 Astra** 등 API 기반 프런티어 모델 대비 비슷하거나 더 나은 성능을 내면서 비용은 약 125배 저렴하다는 점이 차별점이다.

items.title: Every Weight Is a Path of Shared Discrete Decisions
items.abstract: We introduce TWIG (Tree-structured Weights with Inherited Gates), a representation in which every weight of a neural network is the end of a path of small discrete decisions: a sign, a shift by a power of two, a zero gate, an index into a shared table. Weights that belong together share the upper part of their paths, and each decision is inherited by every weight below it, so it is stored once and applied once. This simple change has three consequences. Any trained network can be written as a TWIG, and when the decisions are powers of two its weight layers become circuits made almost entirely of wires and adders, suited to chips whose weights are fixed at fabrication. Pruning, quantization, low-rank factorization, codebooks and weight sharing become edits of one object, so a single optimizer can choose among all of them for a whole network. And choosing the decisions is the ground-state problem of a higher-order Boltzmann machine whose interactions follow the paths of the tree, the problem class that annealers and quantum optimizers are built to solve. Today these questions are handled apart: each compression method brings its own format and solver, a circuit with fixed weights needs a dedicated constant multiplier for every weight, and discrete solvers reach only narrow subproblems such as rounding. Weight formats have long been moving toward shared decisions, through group scales, shared exponents, microexponents and sparse weights; TWIG takes this trend to its end, and every common format is a shallow TWIG at no extra cost. On five weight matrices of a large language model, a flat tree whose signed power-of-two terms are chosen per weight for circuit cost, with no group scales, needs 9--15\% fewer additions than GPTQ at equal layer error at 3- and 4-bit accuracy on typical matrices, and 20--55\% fewer on matrices with strong outliers.
items.title_ko: TWIG: 신경망 가중치를 공유 트리 구조로 표현 — GPTQ 대비 3/4비트에서 덧셈 연산 최대 55% 절감
items.summary: TWIG(Tree-structured Weights with Inherited Gates)는 신경망의 모든 가중치를 부호, 2의 거듭제곱 이동, 제로 게이트, 공유 테이블 인덱스 등 작은 이산 결정들의 경로 끝으로 표현하는 방법이다. 관련된 가중치들은 경로의 상위 부분을 공유해 각 결정이 한 번만 저장·적용되며, 어떤 학습된 네트워크도 TWIG로 변환할 수 있다. 이 구조 덕분에 가지치기, 양자화, 저랭크 분해, 코드북, 가중치 공유 등 서로 다른 압축 기법들이 하나의 객체에 대한 편집으로 통일되어 단일 최적화기로 전체를 다룰 수 있다. 또한 결정을 고르는 문제는 트리 경로를 따르는 고차 볼츠만 머신의 바닥상태 문제로 환원되어 어닐러나 양자 최적화기로 풀 수 있다. 대형 언어모델의 5개 가중치 행렬에 적용한 결과, **GPTQ 대비 3·4비트 정밀도에서 동일한 레이어 오차 기준으로 덧셈 연산이 9~15% 적고, 이상치가 강한 행렬에서는 20~55% 적었다**.
items.why_it_matters: 가중치 압축·양자화·가지치기 등이 제각각의 포맷과 솔버로 다뤄지던 것을 하나의 통일된 표현으로 묶어, 고정 가중치 회로 설계나 이산 최적화 하드웨어(어닐러, 양자 최적화기) 활용 가능성을 열어준다는 점에서 실용적 의미가 크다.
items.whats_different: **기존 GPTQ의 그룹 스케일 기반 양자화 대비** 별도의 그룹 스케일 없이도 가중치별 부호 있는 2의 거듭제곱 항을 선택해 동일 오차에서 더 적은 덧셈 연산으로 회로 비용을 줄인다.
